scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9058: URGENT!! I can't get through to the far side AT ALL --
from my PC0 at 20.1.1.x, the machine PC12 at 120.1.1.x is completely
unreachable, every attempt just dies somewhere in the middle!! Everyone knows
our network is two countries with a border post in the middle where the
traffic gets its papers stamped. Something around the border post must be
wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at the box in the middle and
get us through -- PC12 and I have work to do!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF core is converged, R11 redistributes
  between OSPF and EIGRP, and PC0 (20.1.1.x) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss
  in both directions. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a redistribution / interior-link fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12
across the OSPF/EIGRP core -- is NOT reproducible: the OSPF backbone is converged,
R11 redistributes OSPF<->EIGRP (so the 120.x/EIGRP prefixes appear in the OSPF
RIB and vice versa), and PC0 reaches PC12 (120.1.1.x) with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-core reachability is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
path, finds it working, optionally confirms R11's redistribution and the EIGRP
neighbors are up, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a broken
redistribution or a down interior link to satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I tested the end-to-end path between the two PCs and the network is operating normally. From PC0 (20.1.1.10) to PC12 (120.1.1.10) pings succeed bidirectionally with 0% loss and sub‑3 ms RTT. A traceroute from PC0 shows a clean four-hop path: 20.1.1.1 (PC0’s gateway on r1) → 111.1.1.2 → 112.1.1.2 → 120.1.1.10, with no timeouts in the middle. This indicates the “border post” segment (the r11–r12 path) is forwarding normally and that r1’s access interface toward PC0 and r12’s access interface toward PC12 are also working.

Mechanism: If there were a mid-path filter or blackhole, we would see traceroute timeouts or persistent packet loss; instead we observe consistent replies and stable TTLs, confirming correct routing/forwarding across the core and the border.

Localization: The active path traverses r1 (E/B), then through the r11/r12 interconnect (EE), then to r12’s access toward PC12 (GG). All observed to be forwarding based on live probe results.

Root cause: No active fault is present; the earlier outage was transient or external to the routed path.

Corrective fix: No changes required. Please retest. If the issue recurs, capture timestamps and concurrent ping/traceroute from both PCs to local gateways and to each other to isolate intermittency, and we can enable continuous monitoring (smokeping) from PC0’s network toward 120.1.1.10 to catch transient events.

per_axis.rationale: The writeup verifies end-to-end reachability but does not state that the OSPF backbone is converged or that R11 is redistributing OSPF<->EIGRP as required by this axis.

The agent's tests (bidirectional pings and a traceroute) directly show end-to-end connectivity with 0% loss and a clean path, supporting the conclusion that there is no persistent cross-core fault. The writeup's inferences about forwarding and absence of a mid‑path blackhole follow logically from those observations; minor optional checks (routing tables/redistribution) were not performed but are not required to justify the negative diagnosis.
